purpose.summary: Place the volatile Chronik block projection behind a synchronous Rust single-owner worker without assigning validation or consensus authority.
scope: Move all live observer mutation, rebuild-state reads, and atomic projection adoption onto one named Rust worker thread that exclusively owns the projection.
Use zero-capacity command and response channels plus a producer mutex covering each complete round trip so commands cannot queue or overlap at the state owner.

Exercise the actual Rust worker seam with a bounded unit canary that records the mutation thread, rejects a second send while the first mutation is blocked, verifies response order, and joins the owner cleanly.
Copy each accepted C ABI block payload once into an owned Rust buffer and move it to the worker without a second full Rust-side copy.
Catch Rust unwinds around worker mutations, mark the projection rebuild-required after a post-mutation unwind, and join workers during staging adoption and shutdown.
Preserve compile-time default OFF, runtime default OFF, explicit local-regtest-only opt-in, and observe/index-only operation.
exclusions: No consensus, validation, mempool, chain-selection, activation, chain-parameter, testnet, mainnet, P2P, RPC, wallet, or user-interface rule changes.
No persistence, database, file format, codec, query API, socket, service, asynchronous backlog, or new observed-data semantics.
No claim that rendezvous bounds caller-side buffers copied before producer-mutex acquisition or that Rust unwind handling covers process aborts or foreign exceptions.
No local binary, build cache, raw process output, absolute host path, parent environment, operator material, private history, or unrelated product material enters this change.

files.test_reachability: Defines single-owner, rendezvous, shutdown, panic, and caller-side payload limitations for review.

files.production_reachability: Compiled only in the optional local-regtest observer; one Rust worker owns volatile state and returns no validation decision.
files.test_reachability: Adds synchronous worker lifecycle, ownership transfer, injected post-mutation unwind units, and a bounded canary that records a non-caller mutation owner, observes a second raw send return Full while the first mutation is blocked, verifies exact response-event order, and joins cleanly.

files.production_reachability: Adds a debug startup identity for the optional worker-backed observer; callback semantics and void return authority remain unchanged.
files.test_reachability: Provides a functional startup wiring marker only; the literal log line does not prove mutation ownership or channel capacity.
Requires the executed opt-in binary to emit the expected worker-seam wiring marker before exercising reconstruction; ownership and zero-capacity behavior are proved by the Rust unit canary.

commands: Build with both Chronik options OFF and run inherited legacy mining.
expected_results: No Chronik link edge enters bitcoind and legacy behavior remains unchanged.

commands: Build with BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=ON, omit -chronikobserver, and run mining_basic.py.
expected_results: The optional library is linked but no observer worker starts and inherited mining passes.

commands: Run check-chronik-observer, feature_chronik_block_observer.py, feature_chronik_asset_observer.py, and feature_chronik_pruned_observer.py with --hermetic-child-env on fresh datadirs.
expected_results: Focused units, including the direct ownership/rendezvous canary, and every bounded reconstruction scenario pass through the synchronous worker seam.

scenarios.command: Start the compiled-in observer only on isolated regtest and connect, disconnect, and reconsider confirmed blocks.
expected_results: The startup log confirms the expected worker-seam wiring marker, the Rust unit canary proves the distinct mutation owner and zero-capacity rendezvous behavior, and debug commitments match independent reconstruction while the node tip remains authoritative.
failure_conditions: Any non-regtest activation, missing wiring marker, failed ownership/rendezvous unit canary, commitment mismatch, state mutation on rejection, or validation influence fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: Restart the observer after building a retained active-chain suffix.
expected_results: A staging worker reconstructs the exact ordered retained projection, transfers ownership atomically, and is joined without minting live events.
failure_conditions: Partial adoption, stale state, wrong order, wrong commitment, worker loss, or growth beyond 288 blocks fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: Run a fresh full reindex process at height 288.
expected_results: Ordered block-file callbacks synchronously rebuild the exact last-288-block projection through the single owner.
failure_conditions: Missing, duplicated, reordered, rejected, or mismatched reconstructed observations fail the scenario.

scenarios.command: Run a fresh chainstate reindex process at height 288.
expected_results: Ordered chainstate callbacks rebuild the exact last-288-block projection without changing the active tip or UTXO-set hash.
failure_conditions: Bootstrap masking, block-file reindex, changed chain state, callback divergence, worker loss, or mismatched records fail the scenario.

scenarios.command: Restart explicit observer opt-in on the inherited physically pruned height-1001 datadir.
expected_results: The exact still-readable 288-block suffix reconstructs through staging ownership transfer, and the next connection preserves the bound.
failure_conditions: Unreadable retained bodies, wrong suffix, event minting, record mismatch, worker loss, or bound growth fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: Disconnect through the retained anchor, reject continuation, and restart for reconstruction.
expected_results: Records roll back LIFO, the single owner fails closed beyond its anchor, and restart reconstructs the active suffix.
failure_conditions: Non-LIFO acceptance, mutation after rebuild-required, unbounded retention, worker divergence, or node consensus influence fails the scenario.

platforms: Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 public verification after technical acceptance

limitations: Every validation callback and startup reconstruction request is synchronous; the worker seam isolates ownership but does not reduce callback latency.
The functional startup log is a wiring marker, not proof of thread ownership or rendezvous capacity; those properties are checked directly by the bounded Rust unit canary.
The zero-capacity channel bounds queued worker commands to zero but does not bound one payload already copied by each caller waiting for the producer mutex.
Normal startup transiently creates a separate staging worker, then closes and joins it before moving its projection into the live worker.
Caught Rust unwinds fail the projection closed; process aborts, allocation aborts, and foreign exceptions are outside this mechanism.
No durable state, historical full-chain index, mempool view, query interface, or new observed-data semantics are added.
Local tests are contradiction checks only; no result is public reproduction evidence at record-review time.
counterevidence: No public build or functional execution of the exact candidate exists at record-review time.
The literal C++ startup marker would survive an incorrect worker implementation, so it is not accepted as the ownership or zero-capacity oracle.
A zero-capacity command channel establishes no queued backlog at the worker; it does not establish globally bounded process memory or asynchronous throughput.
A caught injected unwind demonstrates the rebuild-required transition, not recovery from process termination or arbitrary foreign failures.
The unchanged default path remains authoritative: Chronik is compiled out or runtime disabled unless explicitly enabled on local regtest.
